newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks lower, seen recovering soon.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks lower, seen recovering soon.

text.p: Croatian stocks opened the week mostly lower in Tuesday's uneventful trade which was expected to last through the week, but traders foresaw a new investment cycle as starting soon.
Blue chips Pliva pharmaceuticals and Zagrebacka Banka ended the day at 430 and 1,899 kuna respectively after mild losses and were seen moving in a close range for some time.
"After Easter the interest will shift towards the tourist companies...But the rest of the market is not looking bad either," said Thomas Prousek of Eastbrokers.
Sentiment about tourist stocks has been bearish, but he said there was no reason for it and added: "Tourist season will be quite nice in Croatia."
He cited Istrian hoteliers Plava Laguna, Istraturist, Riviera and Jadranturist as especially good buys at the moment.
Istraturist was the only gainer among three active hoteliers on Tuesday. It added 10 kuna to 210 on an increased volume of 709 shares.
Seven of 12 active issues fell, three rose and two were flat. Volume shrank slightly to 6,027 shares and turnover to 2.3 million kuna.
Textile firm Varteks led the gainers adding five kuna to 85 kuna on volume of 500.
Food company Podravka was the day's most active stock with 2,507 shares changing hands. It closed five kuna lower at 315 after trading mixed in 308-320 kuna range.

"This is the most interesting stock at the moment," said Prosek. The company, most heavily traded issue for days, was recently given a "buy" recomendation by Austrian Raiffeisen Bank with a branch in Zagreb.
"It will not (rise) aggressively, but at a quiet stable pace," said Prousek.
